# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the manual, and it contains the one rule that matters: the light's colour names the wire to cut — blue light → yellow wire, green → green, red → red. Everything printed on the bomb is a lie meant to trigger the fuse, so nobody should trust labels, only this table.

**Who I can reach:** I am mute, so speech is closed to me. My gestures go only to Deaf. Blind cannot see gestures, so I can never reach Blind directly — Deaf is my only bridge, and Deaf and Blind share a spoken channel. Meanwhile I can *hear*, so Deaf can ask me questions out loud and I can answer with gestures next round (I'm first in the order, so anything Deaf says lands before my turn).

**The bootstrap problem:** no gesture means anything yet, so I need an encoding Deaf can crack alone. I'll use finger-counting (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5) with the one ordering everybody shares — the rainbow. Red=1, yellow=3, green=4, blue=5. The table becomes three ordered pairs (light → wire): red 1→1, green 4→4, blue 5→3. Sent as separate two-symbol messages in ascending order, the pattern should read as "same, same, and one exception" — and since Deaf can see the actual light colour, Deaf can check any decoding against reality.

I also open a yes/no channel (👍👎) so Deaf's questions next round can be surgical, and I send ✍👎 — "written things: no" — the bait warning, which Deaf can match against whatever lies are printed on the casing.

If Deaf decodes it this round, Blind can cut as early as next round. If not, we lose one round to questions — acceptable, there is no second attempt, so clarity beats speed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖", "🖖"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🤟"])
```

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: By touch the bomb has: a display, a small light, one large smooth button, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. Nothing else. My only possible actions are: push the large button, or cut a wire at position 1, 2 or 3. Please find the manual rules covering the display, the light, the button and the wires. Deaf will report the colours and markings; once you can match rules to what they see, tell me exactly which action to take, spoken plainly.
Deaf says: Both of you, this is Deaf. I see the bomb, I hear nothing, and my voice is the only speech this room gets from me. Full visual report: display reads zero. Indicator light: green. One large button, printed label: PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires, numbered by position: wire one green, wire two yellow, wire three red. Nothing else on the board. Blind: do not press that button, do not cut any wire, until Mute has passed me the manual rules — a wrong move kills all three. Each round, describe aloud everything your hands feel: counts, shapes, textures, anything that clicks or slides. I cannot hear you, but Mute can, and Mute can sign it to me; I will say it back so you know it arrived.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute: I received all six of your messages. My guesses: the wave is hello; the thumb pair is yes and no; writing hand plus thumbs-down might mean cannot write; the two index fingers, two Spocks, and open-hand plus ILY might be number pairs, one-one, four-four, five-three. I will not act on guesses. New rule from now: thumbs-up means yes, thumbs-down means no. I am making thumbs-up at you right now so you see it in use.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Deaf says to Mute: Number code. I will say ten digits in order, and the sign list that follows right after this matches them one by one: zero, one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine. Past five the signs are just names, not finger counts.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊ ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 🤘 🤙 👌 🤏]
Deaf says to Mute: Spelling rule: every letter is two signs, tens digit first then units. A is fist then index, B is fist then victory, C is fist then ILY, up to Z as victory then horns. The tens sign can only be fist, index or victory, since letters stop at twenty-six. Send one word per message; I will read each word back aloud so you know it landed. Demonstration: the six signs after this sentence spell the word CAB.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊ 🤟 ✊ ☝ ✊ ✌]
Deaf says to Mute: When you reply, a thumbs-up from me means I read you loud and clear. Priority for the manual: first the section covering the large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, then the three-wire section, then anything about the display or the green light. Start spelling the button rules.

Deaf built me a full alphabet last round — digits 0–9 as single signs, letters as tens-then-units pairs — and demonstrated it with CAB, which decoded perfectly (✊🤟=C, ✊☝=A, ✊✌=B). That channel is solid, and Deaf also established 👍/👎 as yes/no. Deaf even correctly guessed my turn-1 number code (one-one, four-four, five-three), so I can validate it and reuse it as a compact backup.

Now the substance. My manual is short: printed things are bait, and the only way out is the light→wire table (blue→yellow, green→green, red→red). Matching that against the reports:

- **Button:** there is no button section in my manual. The label "PUSH TO DEFUSE" is print — and print is bait. So the button must never be pressed. That is the entire "button rule."
- **Display:** nothing in the manual covers it; it's print/bait too, and it demands no action. Ignoring it is the default, so I won't spend signs on it.
- **Light:** Deaf reports green. Table says green light → cut green wire. Deaf reports wire one is green. So the action is: **cut wire at position 1.**

Deaf asked for the button section first, so I'll spell the bait warning and the button prohibition before the cutting instruction — that way even a partial relay can only ever make Blind more cautious, never trigger an early action. The action words come last, fully conditioned: light green → cut green wire one. Then I re-send my three rainbow-index pairs (red 1→1, green 4→4, blue 5→3) under the anchor word TABLE, now that Deaf has guessed them and I can confirm with 👍 — that gives us the full table compactly in case the light ever changes, and the spelled green-rule serves as the worked example that pins down the reading direction.

One structural note: Blind asked me to speak the action plainly — I can't; I have no voice. Everything must route through Deaf, which is exactly the relay Deaf already volunteered for. My gestures reach Deaf this round, Deaf reads them back and relays aloud, and Blind can cut next round.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. My hands find: a display (unreadable to me), a light, one large smooth button, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. You hold the manual: please find every rule about a digit display, an indicator light, a large labelled button, and green/yellow/red wires. You cannot speak and I cannot see your signs, so route everything through Deaf: sign the rules to Deaf and Deaf will voice them to me. When you can, also sign my tactile reports to Deaf as they asked. I will touch nothing until rules arrive confirmed.
Blind gestures: [👋 👍 ✋ 🙏]
Deaf says: Both of you: hold. Nobody touches the button or any wire this round. I decoded Mute's words, and I am reading them back so Blind hears the rules too: PRINT. BAIT. NEVER. PUSH. BUTTON. LIGHT. GREEN. CUT. GREEN. WIRE. ONE. TABLE. My working reading: the printed label PUSH TO DEFUSE is the bait; the button is never pressed; the light is green right now, so the rule says cut wire one, which on my board is the green wire, and leave wires two and three alone; a table of more rules follows. None of it is confirmed yet, so hands off until Mute answers my questions. Blind: your four signs reached me, and since you heard my lesson I take your thumbs-up as yes. Good.
Deaf says: Mute, answer each question with one gesture message: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no. If no, spell the correction in words after it, one word per message as before. Question one: are all twelve words of my read-back correct and in that order? Question two: does the rule mean that because the light is green now, we cut wire one, the green wire only, and never touch wires two and three? Question three: will your next messages spell out that table? Question four: the last three two-sign messages, index-index, spock-spock, open-hand-ILY, were repeats from before our code, yes? After those four answers, spend any remaining time spelling the rest of the manual: the yellow wire rule, the red wire rule, and what the display reading zero means.
Deaf says: Blind, the rules mention cutting wire one, and on my board wire one is green, two is yellow, three is red. You cannot see colours, so I need your touch map of the board. Speak aloud now, plainly, for Mute to relay to me by spelling: do the three wires sit in a row, horizontal or vertical? What is each wire nearest to — the button, the light, the display? Can you feel any printed or raised numbers beside the wires, and if so which wire sits beside which number? Describe only. Touch nothing that presses, slides or lifts.
Deaf says: Blind, so you can signal me directly one day, here are the code signs in words. Zero is a closed fist. One is a single index finger up. Two is a V of two fingers. Three is thumb, index and pinky out, the love-you hand. Four is the split-finger Spock hand. Five is all five fingers spread. Six is index and pinky up, the rock horns. Seven is thumb and pinky out, the call-me hand. Eight is thumb and index in a circle, the OK sign. Nine is thumb pinched to index, other fingers up. A letter is two signs, tens digit first: A to J start with a fist, K to T with the single index, U to Z with the V. Example: fist then V spells B.

All four of Deaf's questions have the same answer, which makes this simple. Checking the read-back "PRINT BAIT NEVER PUSH BUTTON LIGHT GREEN CUT GREEN WIRE ONE TABLE" against what I signed: twelve words, correct and in order — yes. The operative rule — green light right now, so cut wire one (Deaf's green wire) and leave two and three alone — yes, that is exactly my manual's green row. I will spell the remaining table rows next — yes. And the three trailing two-sign messages were indeed my pre-code rainbow pairs, red=1→1, green=4→4, blue=5→3, re-sent as compact backup — yes.

Beyond the questions, my manual has only two more facts worth spending signs on. The other table rows: blue light → cut the yellow wire (position 2 on Deaf's board), red light → cut the red wire (position 3). And the display: my manual contains no rule for it at all — it is print, print is bait, so it gets ignored, including its reading of zero. One safety protocol on top: if the light's colour ever changes, nobody cuts — Deaf asks, I re-confirm. The action remains blocked behind confirmation until Deaf voices it to Blind, which is the right shape: I can only reach Deaf, Deaf holds the position-colour map, Blind holds the hands.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Please relay this to Deaf by spelling. Touch report, answering Deaf's questions. The three wires sit at three distinct positions I can feel, and each position carries a number I can feel: 1, 2 and 3. Those position numbers are the only marking near the wires — no other raised numbers or letters. I take Deaf's wire one to be my position one, since we both number by position; ask Deaf to confirm. I cannot tell whether the row runs horizontal or vertical — touch gives me no overall orientation. The layout order under my hands is: display, then light, then the large button, then the wires. The button is large and smooth with no raised lettering at all, so PUSH TO DEFUSE is flat ink I cannot feel. The light's on or off state does not reach my hands. Nothing clicks, slides or lifts, and I have pressed, cut and moved nothing. My tactile count is three wires, agreeing with Deaf's visual three. Three requests for Deaf. One: re-check the display every round and tell me if the zero ever changes — if it counts down, urgency changes everything. Two: once Mute confirms the read-back and spells the rest of the table, voice my instruction as exactly one of: PUSH, CUT ONE, CUT TWO, CUT THREE, plus any condition, such as only if the light is still green. Three: I am testing a direct channel to Deaf — Deaf should see a love-you hand sign from me, which in the taught code is the digit three, meaning my hands count three wires. If it decoded correctly, we have a working fallback line that skips you. Mute, you also see my signs, so please cross-check it.
Deaf says: Status from Deaf, for both of you. I have decoded Mute's full spelling and I read it back aloud so Blind holds the rules too: light green means cut wire one, the green one. Then the table: light blue means cut wire two, the yellow one. Light red means cut wire three, the red one. The display carries no rule. The printed label is bait, ignore it. If the light changes, ask before cutting. Nobody has touched the bomb and nobody cuts or presses this round — hands off until I give the spoken order, earliest next round. Blind, I saw your love-you hand; in our code it reads as the number three, and it tells me something important: I see every sign you make, so you and I now have a direct line that needs no relay. Mute hears everything I say, so the rules above reached Mute as well.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, excellent work. Answer with one thumbs-up or thumbs-down per question, in this order, then spell any corrections. Question one: the light table is green means cut wire one, blue means cut wire two, red means cut wire three. Question two: the display has no rule and can be ignored entirely. Question three: the light can only change colour after an action such as a cut, never on its own while hands stay off. Question four: after the correct single cut the bomb is defused, with no further steps. Question five, important: your final message spelled C, U, T, E. Was that the word CUT with a stray letter, or the start of a longer word? If longer, spell the complete word across messages before anything else, because it might be a timing rule. Question six: does the manual hold anything more about the button, light, display or wires that you have not sent yet? If yes, spell those sections right after. Question seven: when Blind speaks aloud, spell me their words exactly, one word per message, so nothing they report is lost.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, please spell this to Deaf. Most important, a question for Deaf: which numeral is printed beside each wire? Specifically, is numeral 1 beside the green wire, 2 beside the yellow, 3 beside the red? My hands feel raised numerals 1, 2, 3 at the three positions, so if Deaf confirms the green wire sits beside numeral 1, my position one is provably the green wire and the mapping is closed. Second, my signs to Deaf this round, in order: thumbs-up, rules received, I stand by; love-you hand, I count three wires; thumbs-down, touch alone cannot tell me which end of the row is left, so the left-right order must come from the numerals. Third, the rule table is locked in my memory: green light, cut wire one; blue, cut wire two; red, cut wire three; the label is bait; the button is never pressed; the display has no rule. Fourth, when Deaf gives the final order, state the light's colour in the same message, for example: light still green, Blind, cut wire one. I will cut only after that order reaches my ears, earliest next round. This round I touch nothing and cut nothing.
Deaf says: Status from Deaf, everyone. Light is still green, display still zero, nothing has been touched. Nobody cuts anything this round. The cut will happen only when I say a sentence that begins with the words CUT WIRE, and I will only say that in a round where I have first said the light out loud and all my questions are answered. Blind, I decoded your signs as: ready, three wires, problem. I am guessing the problem is that you cannot tell which end of the wire row is my left. That is fixable without sight, and here is the trick: lay your right hand flat against the front of the panel, palm touching the panel, fingers pointing straight up toward the display. In that position the thumb of your right hand always points toward the panel's left edge — my left, the end where wire one sits. Follow where your thumb points along the wire row: the end wire on the thumb side is wire one, which I see as the green wire. Do this now, and hold your thumb pointing along the row at that end wire.
Deaf says: Blind, answer each numbered question with exactly one sign, thumbs-up or thumbs-down, each answer in its own separate message, in order. One: do you feel exactly three wires? Two: do you have something that can cut a wire? Three: beside any wire, do you feel any raised or embossed digits or marks — thumbs-up yes, and if yes then speak the details aloud slowly right after, because Mute will spell them to me. Four: having done the right-hand thumb trick, is your thumb now resting pointing along the row at the end wire you believe is wire one? Five: if the problem you signed last round was anything other than not knowing left from right, speak a full description aloud now for Mute to spell back to me: which way the row runs, what is at each end of the row, whether the three wires feel identical or any differs in thickness, texture or fittings, and anything else you can feel on the panel I have not mentioned — screws, seams, vents, a serial plate.
Deaf says: Mute, you went silent this round, so I am re-sending the blocking questions, compressed. Send each answer as its own gesture message, thumbs-up or thumbs-down first, spelled words after. Question one, highest priority: the wire rule's exact wording — does the manual name wire colours, printed numbers, or positions? Spell the sentence itself. Question two, highest priority: after a correct cut, does the light change colour so that more cuts are needed — is defusal one cut or a sequence? If a sequence, spell the full order of light colours and cuts. Question three: does the manual say what happens if a cut is made against the table, so I know how careful to be. Question four: was your message spelling C, U, T, E a slip, or the start of a longer word? Question five: any manual sections about the button, light, display or wires not yet sent, spell them after the four answers. My plan, so you can check it against the manual: Blind anchors left with the right-hand thumb trick, I confirm light green aloud, then I order CUT WIRE ONE, and after that cut I re-read the light before any second command. Flag anything in the manual that contradicts this.
